paper.title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action
paper.central_claim: A navigation system assembled only from frozen pre-trained models (GPT-3 landmark extraction, CLIP grounding on a topological graph, ViNG navigation model, graph search over a joint likelihood) follows free-form outdoor instructions on a real wheeled robot without fine-tuning or language-annotated robot data; 85% of 20 queries (over 6 km) succeeded.

status_reason: full text with appendices A-E read; in-scope (frozen LLM+VLM harness with a navigation controller on a real mobile robot)

evidence.quote: we show that such a system can be constructed entirely out of pre-trained models for navigation (ViNG), image-language association (CLIP), and language modeling (GPT-3), without requiring any fine-tuning or language-annotated robot data
The LLM and VLM queries are pre-computed on a remote workstation and the computed path is commanded to the robot wirelessly.
evidence.support_explanation: plan computed before execution; open-loop w.r.t. LLM/VLM

evidence.quote: In each evaluation environment, we first construct the graph by manually driving the robot and collecting image and GPS observations.
We tested our system on 20 queries, in environments of varying difficulty, corresponding to a total combined length of over 6 km.
LM-Nav can consistently follow the instructions in 85% of the experiments, without collisions or disengagements (an average of 1 intervention per 6.4km of traversals).
In all the unsuccessful experiments, the failure can be attributed to the inability of the planning stage
evidence.support_explanation: all failures are planning (landmark detection) failures

evidence.quote: A walk produced by the graph search is considered successful , if (1) it matches the path intended by the user or (2) if the landmark images extracted by the search algorithm indeed contain said landmarks
evidence.support_explanation: success criterion for planning; judge of 'contain said landmarks' not stated

signatures.object: Instruction-to-walk pipeline: landmark list -> node probabilities -> graph walk -> VNM execution
signatures.information: free-form text; topological graph of images+GPS collected beforehand in the target environment; VNM temporal-distance estimates; LLM/VLM see no embodiment; plan computed off-board
signatures.operation: GPT-3 (3-example prompt) extracts ordered landmarks; CLIP scores every node for each landmark (softmax over nodes); dynamic programming / Dijkstra maximizes sum of CLIP scores minus alpha x distance
signatures.output: walk of graph nodes executed by the on-board VNM policy
signatures.conditions: landmarks exist and are CLIP-recognizable; graph connectivity correct; robot-specific VNM
signatures.feedback: none during execution at the LLM/VLM level (no replanning); VNM provides distances/actions
signatures.selection_data: no data; alpha/gamma not reported in the pinned text
signatures.persistence: graph reused for any instruction in that environment
signatures.claimed_effect: 85% of 20 queries without disengagement; planning success 0.9/0.8 vs 0.6/0.2 for max-likelihood planner
signatures.failure_boundary: missing or undetectable landmarks (fire hydrant, cement mixer), verbs/commands ignored, variable binding in CLIP

signatures.information: images, GPS, timestamps from manual driving; VNM distance predictions
signatures.operation: connect nodes within 1-2 s in time or with small VNM distance and GPS-consistent; drop wormholes; transitive reduction
signatures.claimed_effect: makes planning over past experience possible
signatures.failure_boundary: aliased observations (white walls, fields) create wormholes

gap.author_gap: language-instructed navigation either needs expensive language-annotated trajectories or unnatural goal specification (images/GPS) for self-supervised policies
gap.checked_gap: reasonable and concrete; the paper does not run a quantitative comparison to VLN or annotated-instruction baselines, so the claim of avoiding annotation is argued, not benchmarked

closest_adjacent.note: needs text-conditioned skills; LM-Nav avoids language-annotated robot data
assume a low-level agent that executes textual instructions

lineage.method_note: local texts only; no external search

gap.residue: landmark-only grounding, VLM failures on hard landmarks, robot-specific VNM, pre-collected graph, no execution-time replanning or LLM involvement
gap.stakes: removes annotation cost from language-conditioned navigation
gap.method_response: pre-trained LLM/VLM supply language and grounding while a self-supervised VNM supplies control and a graph search fuses them
gap.remaining_gap: accuracy of open-vocabulary landmark detection and portability beyond the Jackal VNM (E015, E017)
unresolved: comparison to annotation-based VLN on the same routes

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop real-robot runs with counts (20 queries) whose success depends on actual traversal; the plan is computed once and the environments and prompts were part of development, one embodiment, so not transfer
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 20 author-designed outdoor instructions in two environments that were pre-traversed, a Jackal robot using frozen GPT-3, CLIP and ViNG with graph search followed the intended landmark sequence in about 85% of runs with one intervention in 6 km
assessment.author_claim_kept: annotation-free long-horizon instruction following in complex outdoor environments
unresolved: comparison to annotated-VLN or SayCan-style baselines

G.reason: clear, sourced gap (annotation cost vs unnatural goal specification) with named neighbors (SayCan, Huang et al., VLN) but no quantitative comparison with them; residue (landmark-only, platform-specific, pre-explored map) is stated honestly

M.reason: probabilistic formulation with explicit factors (landmark likelihood x discounted traversal) yields distinguishable predictions confirmed by the max-likelihood and GPS ablations; weak points: softmax over nodes forces probability mass onto absent landmarks (acknowledged), alpha/gamma unspecified, variable-binding explanation untested

X.reason: pipeline, prompts, graph-building thresholds and search algorithm are given; information access and failure boundaries are clear; missing numeric alpha/gamma and the LLM/VLM-in-loop assumption (no replanning, plan computed off-board) limit exact reconstruction

measurement.reason: real traversal with disengagement counts and path efficiency, but success for planning is judged by an unstated rater, every query ran once, and the extracted Table 1 is inconsistent with the 85% text (anchors v2: single trials cap at 2)

causality.reason: four one-at-a-time ablations (VNM, search objective, LLM, VLM) on the same queries; GPT-3's perfect score is on the 20 test prompts, no end-to-end baseline from another paradigm, variable-binding story untested

holdout.reason: graph built and queries chosen in the evaluation environments, VLM test landmarks drawn from the same instructions, prompt tuned on instruction types, one robot

statistics.reason: single run per query, 10 per environment, no variance, ambiguous table; failure attribution is only qualitative

cost.reason: no latency, token, call-count or compute figure for GPT-3/CLIP queries, graph building or search; budgets of ablations not stated
